summary: Facepalm: Facepalm scan for 2026-10-02 (window Sept 26 – Oct 2). I'm submitting no candidates: nothing I found met every rule. Most of the institutional blunders I turned up were either outside the window or covered only by outlets not on the accepted list. Several were already published or already set aside. The search budget ran out partway through the scan, and the one in-window follow-up from an accepted outlet (Texas Tribune, Oct. 1) couldn't be opened. Genius: Genius scan for 2026-10-02. My search budget ran out early, and later the page-fetch budget did too, so the shortlist is thin. I'm submitting two candidates, and both rely on an official page plus ScienceDaily. (1) NASA said on Sept. 30 that the Roman Space Telescope passed its fine-guidance tests and that its coronagraph saw light for the first time. This is a commissioning milestone, so the verifier may judge it too routine to count as an achievement. (2) NC State's Plant Armor fabric raised strawberry yields up to 3.56 times in tunnel field tests. NC State announced it Sept. 29, but the journal paper came out Sept. 25, one day before the strict 7-day window, so it may fail on freshness. The strongest lead I found was Crew-13 setting a record for the fastest U.S. trip to the ISS on Oct. 1. I couldn't submit it: the only post-docking coverage I could open was from Space.com, and I had no budget left to find a second publisher. Several other leads were too old or not US-led. No facepalm story met the standard; nothing published. The verified genius story is on the bench for a later day.

candidates.headline: NASA's Roman Space Telescope passes pointing tests and its coronagraph sees cosmic light for the first time
candidates.reason: passed every check; kept for a later day because the other side had no story

candidates.headline: NC State researchers' 'Plant Armor' fabric raises strawberry yields up to 3.56 times in field tests
candidates.reason: an earlier candidate was published

candidates.headline: Texas DPS error leaves tens of thousands of voter registration applications unprocessed
candidates.reason: The error was first reported Sept. 22, before the window, and the Votebeat piece I opened was published Sept. 25. The one in-window follow-up (Texas Tribune, Oct. 1, on delays flagged months earlier) couldn't be fetched. The story is also about voters possibly losing their registrations, which is closer to harm than a self-contained blunder.

candidates.headline: Knox County, Ind., voting machines re-programmed a third time over ballot error
candidates.reason: In the window (Oct. 2), but the only coverage found was WWBL, WZDM, the Vincennes Sun-Commercial and WTWO/MyWabashValley, none on the accepted list. The WWBL page couldn't be opened.

candidates.headline: California voter guides mailed with pages 57–120 missing after printer error
candidates.reason: In the window (Sept. 29), but the only source found was KESQ, which isn't on the accepted list. The Secretary of State's office said only two voters had reported it.

candidates.headline: Maine Senate nominee Troy Jackson apologizes for remarks about Jewish Mainers' views on Gaza
candidates.reason: The story is about remarks concerning a religious group, which the rules exclude. It's also about a candidate's views, not a concrete act in office.

candidates.headline: Nassau County Republican mailers attribute a quote to Democrats who say they never said it
candidates.reason: Republican subject, which the current balance rule doesn't allow. Coverage is also dated after the scan date.

candidates.headline: Maine 'packaging error' sends wrong ballots to some Oxford County voters
candidates.reason: Reported Oct. 7, after the scan date.

candidates.headline: Pender County, N.C., sends incorrect property tax bills
candidates.reason: Reported Oct. 6, after the scan date. The only source found (Port City Daily) isn't on the accepted list.

candidates.headline: 300 wrong mail-in ballots sent to two Kendall County, Ill., precincts
candidates.reason: Reported Oct. 9, after the scan date. The only source found (Shaw Local) isn't an accepted publisher.

candidates.headline: SpaceX Crew-13 docks at the ISS 7 hours 55 minutes after launch, the fastest trip by a U.S. spacecraft
candidates.reason: Inside the window (Oct. 1, Florida), but Space.com was the only accepted publisher I could open with post-docking coverage. The ScienceDaily pages are pre-launch NASA advisories that only predict a record. My search and fetch budgets ran out before I could find a second outlet. Worth retrying.

candidates.headline: Stanford chemist Song Lin named 2026 MacArthur Fellow
candidates.reason: Announced Sept. 29, inside the window, but the only page I opened was Stanford's own release. The NPR list pages are blocked from fetching, and the other coverage I found (C&EN, Harvard Magazine, Stanford Daily, Yahoo) is not on the accepted list.

candidates.headline: ASU-led study finds black hole jets light up gas far beyond their galaxies
candidates.reason: Too old. ASU's release is dated Sept. 24, before the window. Space.com (Oct. 2) and ScienceDaily (Sept. 30) only came later.

candidates.headline: Cornell team finds human brain gene BC200 can still jump through DNA
candidates.reason: Too old. According to the Cornell release, the Science paper came out Sept. 24, and ScienceDaily's write-up is dated Oct. 5, after the scan date.

candidates.headline: Oregon State light-activated material makes hydrogen from water
candidates.reason: The only accepted news page, from ScienceDaily, is dated Oct. 4, after the scan date. I couldn't confirm the JACS publication date.

candidates.headline: UT Austin dates buried Oklahoma impact crater 100 million years later than thought
candidates.reason: Too old. The paper came out in July in Meteoritics & Planetary Science, and the ScienceDaily page is dated Oct. 4.

candidates.headline: MEGATRON simulations show how the first stars changed the universe
candidates.reason: Not US-led: the project is led by the University of Bath in the UK, with UChicago as a collaborator.

candidates.headline: ALMA images twin planets forming around WISPIT 2
candidates.reason: Not US-led: according to Space.com, the image and analysis came from MPIA in Germany.

candidates.headline: Superfluid-helium qubit proposed to cut quantum errors 100-fold
candidates.reason: Not in the US: the work came from the University of Surrey in the UK.

candidates.headline: Megan Eckert sets women's 6-day running world record
candidates.reason: The only source found was iRunFar, which is not an accepted publisher, and the race location was not confirmed to be in the US.
